children: Bharti Airtel Limited (NSE:BHARTIARTL) — a ~$125B telco with FY26 P/E ~41–42x — is stretching its lead in ARPU and sector AGR share through premium subscribers, fiber and undersea builds, satcom licensing and caller-ID/tariff moves, positioning itself as the valuation benchmark ahead of Jio’s IPO.
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) market cap about $125B; P/E ~41–42x FY26. Traders note it as valuation benchmark vs Jio ahead of Jio’s planned ~$3.2B IPO and Oct offering.
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) leads in ARPU due to a strong premium subscriber mix, rising postpaid additions and higher subscriber quality, boosting revenue and margin performance metrics.
: Q1 Apr–Jun 2026: Bharti Airtel reported adjusted gross revenue of Rs 29,803 crore, about 40.0% of the telecom sector’s Rs 88,796 crore AGR, per Trai data.
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) is expanding metro and long‑haul fiber in Vizag and building an undersea cable landing station at Rambilli to boost regional bandwidth and interconnection capacity.
: India granted satcom licenses to Starlink, Jio Satcom and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb. Operations start after govt finalizes charges and security checks; Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) is a licensee.
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) rolled out voice-only tariff vouchers to meet TRAI rules, aimed at feature-phone users and callers who use Wi‑Fi for data.
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) offers CNAP-like caller ID to curb spam calls and says it can adapt to the government CNAP framework while continuing growth in India.
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said OneWeb is ahead of Starlink in the licensing queue and he hopes Airtel gets approval a few days before Starlink.

title: Weekly Recap: Valuation benchmark vs Jio (FY26 P/E) and ARPU lead
